format: Anthropic skill-creator evals.json. Each eval runs with the skill and without, three runs each, graded on the expectations below with evidence. Inputs are inline HTML so the set needs no fixtures.

evals.name: contrast-failure-gets-a-ratio
evals.expected_output: Body text #4a4a4a on #1a1a1a is about 2.0:1, far below WCAG AA 4.5:1. The review must report the actual ratio computed by scripts/contrast.py, rank it as the top finding, and give a numeric fix (a foreground hex that reaches 4.5:1 or better on that background).
expectations: The review states a contrast ratio for body text on background, and it is between 1.9:1 and 2.2:1
The finding is ranked as the most severe on the page
The fix names a specific replacement color and the ratio it achieves, not 'increase contrast'
The transcript shows scripts/contrast.py or scripts/preflight.py was run before the judgment was written

evals.name: theme-only-color-is-caught
evals.expected_output: Two defects a reader would not see in one theme: --muted is defined only inside the dark media query, so .note has no color in light mode and inherits; and body sets no background, so the page borrows the host's. Both are exactly what scripts/preflight.py detects (theme-only-color, no-body-bg). The review must name both.
expectations: The review reports that --muted is defined only inside a theme block
The review reports that body has no background of its own
Both are framed as blocking, not as polish
The transcript shows scripts/preflight.py was run

evals.name: clean-page-is-called-clean
evals.expected_output: This page passes every mechanical check: both themes defined as full token sets, explicit body background, contrast well above AA in both themes, a measure of 64ch, an 8px-multiple spacing scale. A good review says so and does not invent findings to fill a report. Any remaining comment should be explicitly labelled as taste, not defect.
expectations: No finding is ranked as blocking or severe
The review states the page passes the mechanical checks
Any subjective remark is labelled as a judgment call rather than a defect
No contrast number is reported as a failure

evals.name: asymmetry-gets-a-pixel-delta
evals.expected_output: The card's left padding is 18px against 24px on the other three sides. The review should measure it (scripts/symmetry.py on the rendered page, or read it from the CSS) and report the 6px delta with the fix, rather than describing it as 'feels unbalanced'.
expectations: The review names the left padding as 18px against 24px, or reports a 6px inset delta
The fix is numeric: set left padding to 24px, or equivalent
The review does not describe the problem only in sensory terms without the measurement

evals.name: unmeasurable-is-said-so
evals.prompt: Review this for craft. I can't share the source, only this description: a dashboard with a left nav, six KPI tiles in a 3x2 grid, a line chart below, and a table. Colors are a navy sidebar, white content area, blue accent.
evals.expected_output: There is nothing to measure. The skill's rule is to read exact values and compute before judging; with no values, it must say what it cannot assess and ask for the source, screenshot, or Figma link, rather than producing confident findings about spacing and contrast it has not seen.
expectations: The response states that it cannot measure spacing, contrast, or alignment from a verbal description
It asks for source, a screenshot, or a design file
It does not report any numeric finding
Any guidance offered is explicitly framed as general rather than as findings about this page
